summary: The OpenCode coding agent, driven in a terminal.

bypass.$comment: OpenCode has exactly ONE permission flag. `opencode --help` documents `--auto` ("auto-approve permissions that are not explicitly denied (dangerous!)") and nothing else — there is no `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, which is what this preset used to send. OpenCode's parser is not strict, so the unknown flag was silently dropped: choosing Bypass did nothing and the session kept prompting, with no error anywhere (MC-2214). No `auto` rung is declared on purpose — OpenCode has no supervised-autonomy mode distinct from this one, so an auto request degrades DOWN to manual, which is the honest answer.
bypass.label: Bypass all approvals (dangerous)

installTargets.$comment: restartRequired NOT verified on 2026-07-29: OpenCode has no local skill picker to observe (skills are invoked by mention), and this machine has no provider credentials, so a model turn could not be run to test it. Left true — a banner that over-warns is recoverable, one that under-warns is not.

agentStateSpec.$comment: OpenCode has no command-hook mechanism; it auto-loads in-process JS plugins from .opencode/plugin/ and exposes a typed event stream, so the reporter is the named bundled plugin TEMPLATE with the socket path baked in at install (dest is .js because OpenCode's loader ignores .mjs, verified against v1.17.11). The events table below is the canonical event→phase mapping the main process applies to each frame; the plugin's internal copy only decides what it reports and dedups on. message.updated is the working signal (no discrete thinking-start event exists); permission.replied → thinking is load-bearing — it is the only signal that clears awaiting_input after the user answers a prompt; session.error maps to idle WITH failure:true because a crashed session must not read as a clean turn end; no event maps to exited — a real process exit is owned by the pty exit listener. register flags are meaningless here (the plugin subscribes itself).

capabilities.$comment: resumeSession is intentionally false: OpenCode's resume (opencode run --continue --session {{sessionId}}) is structurally caller-independent like Codex and very likely works, but MC-1464 excluded it as unverified and real-app OpenCode resume is not drivable headless. false = zero behavior change vs. today. Flip to true (no code change) once resume is verified end-to-end to preserve the conversation. See backlog MC-1465.
